summary: A message containing a newline can no longer put its words in another member's mouth: every transcript render now collapses a message to one line.
details: Nora's prompt renders the room as one line per message — a handle, how long ago it was sent, the sender's name, then what they said. A message that contained a line break was rendered as written, so its second line arrived with no sender on it, directly above somebody else's. She read the tail of one person's message as part of another's, which is the long-standing 'she quoted the wrong person' report.

The same gap let a member write a whole fake message into the transcript, choosing the name on it. A line typed as part of an ordinary message was indistinguishable from a real one — including a line attributed to Nora herself, asserting something she never said.

Eight places were affected and all eight are fixed: the reply prompt (for a tag and for a reminder), the debrief fold, the note curator's evidence and her own sends, the note-candidate index, the proactive standing listing, and the two review surfaces an operator reads verdicts off. The check that decides whether a quiet room is worth her turn was fixed two days ago and is where the problem was found; the other eight were never looked at. Three of them write durable state, so a fake line could settle a note or a position and outlive the turn that read it.
Nothing is dropped. The full text of every message still reaches her, still quoted and still read — only the line break becomes a space, which is what a reader would have seen anyway.
limitations: A message whose own formatting carried meaning in line breaks — a list, a pasted block — now reaches her as one line. The whole text is there; the shape is not.

The message she is directly replying to, and her own folded position on a room, are each rendered whole between their own tags rather than as one line among many, so their paragraph breaks are preserved.
